Class ZipWriter

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.runner.build.ZipWriter
All Implemented Interfaces:
Closeable, AutoCloseable
public final class ZipWriter extends Object implements Closeable
A minimal ZIP writer that only ever writes STORED entries and reports the absolute offset of every entry's data as it goes.

Both properties are what the runner jar format is built on. Because nothing is deflated, an entry's bytes lie contiguously in the outer file and the launcher can define a class straight from a memory-mapped slice, or hand out a nested jar's bytes without copying them. Because the offset of the data is returned by the write call itself, the packager never has to parse back what it just wrote to fill in IndexFormat.E_DATA_OFFSET.

Timestamps are fixed: every entry gets the MS-DOS time derived from the Instant handed to the constructor, converted in UTC so that the same inputs produce a byte-identical archive on any machine. The default is DEFAULT_TIMESTAMP, which is in 1980 because MS-DOS time cannot represent anything earlier. ZipRepacker overrides it per entry to preserve a dependency's original times.

ZIP64 records are written when the archive needs them: a ZIP64 end of central directory record and locator from 65535 entries upwards, or once the central directory reaches 4 GiB in size or in offset, and a ZIP64 extended information extra field on the records of entries whose size or local header offset does not fit in 32 bits. Every field that is replaced by a 64-bit value in an extra field carries the IndexFormat.ZIP64_MARKER value in its 32-bit slot, as the specification requires.

Instances are not thread-safe. close() finishes the archive if finish() was not called and closes the underlying stream.

  • Field Details

    • DEFAULT_TIMESTAMP

      public static final Instant DEFAULT_TIMESTAMP
      The timestamp given to every entry unless the caller supplies another one: 1980-02-01T00:00:00Z.

      The MS-DOS date field cannot represent a year before 1980, so the usual 1970 epoch is unusable; the first of February keeps the value clear of any time zone rounding into 1979.

    • ZipWriter

      public ZipWriter(OutputStream out, Instant timestamp, boolean uniqueNames)
      Creates a writer using a fixed timestamp for every entry, choosing how strict duplicate detection is.

      The outer archive is built from scratch and must reject a repeated name, and a name that differs from another only by case, because it has to behave the same when it is unpacked on a case-insensitive file system. A dependency jar being repacked is a different matter: both are legal in a jar somebody else produced - zip -g and some shading pipelines emit them - and a build must not fail over an input that java.util.zip.ZipFile reads without complaint. The index keys on the record rather than on a set of names, so a repeated name simply becomes a same-name chain, exactly as it does in the PRESERVE compression mode where the jar is copied verbatim. ZipRepacker therefore relaxes both checks.

      Parameters:
      out - the stream the archive is written to
      timestamp - the instant every entry is dated with, converted in UTC
      uniqueNames - whether a repeated name, or one differing from another only by case, is an error
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if an argument is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if the instant is outside the range MS-DOS time can represent

    • toDosTime

      public static int toDosTime(Instant timestamp)
      Converts an instant to the MS-DOS date and time layout the ZIP format stores, the date in the high 16 bits and the time in the low 16 bits.

      The conversion is done in UTC rather than in the default time zone, which is what makes the output independent of the machine that produced it.

      Parameters:
      timestamp - the instant to convert
      Returns:
      the MS-DOS date and time, in the layout IndexFormat.E_DOS_TIME expects
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if timestamp is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if the year is before 1980 or after 2107, which MS-DOS time cannot represent

    • writeEntry

      public long writeEntry(String name, InputStream source, long length, long crc32, int dosTime) throws IOException
      Writes a file entry by streaming exactly length bytes from a source.

      The size and CRC-32 have to be known in advance because a stored entry's local file header carries them and this writer never emits a data descriptor.

      Parameters:
      name - the entry name, which must be safe and must not end with '/'
      source - the content, read but not closed
      length - the exact number of bytes to copy
      crc32 - the CRC-32 of those bytes, as an unsigned 32-bit value
      dosTime - the MS-DOS date and time to store
      Returns:
      the absolute offset of the entry's first data byte
      Throws:
      IOException - if the name is unsafe or duplicated, the source ends early, or the stream cannot be written

    • writeEntry

      public long writeEntry(String name, Path source) throws IOException
      Writes a file entry from a file, reading it twice: once to compute its CRC-32 and once to copy it.

      This is how a nested jar built into a temporary file is added to the outer archive without ever holding it in memory.

      Parameters:
      name - the entry name, which must be safe and must not end with '/'
      source - the file to store
      Returns:
      the absolute offset of the entry's first data byte
      Throws:
      IOException - if the name is unsafe or duplicated, or either file cannot be read or written
